run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The social-network front end is down: pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-dw5sd is the only Ready=False pod in namespace social-network, its openresty-thrift container exits with code 137 about 4 s after each start (twice: 09:45:11-09:45:15Z and 09:45:16-09:45:19Z, restartCount 1, kubelet BackOff), and the nginx-thrift Service has only notReadyAddresses, so the front end has no usable backend. The pod's container carries requests.memory=16Mi and limits.memory=16Mi although its owner ReplicaSet template declares 128Mi/256Mi, and it is the only one of the 27 pods in the namespace with any memory limit; that 16Mi value equals the MEMORY constant hard-coded in the platform-policy-controller webhook backend and was applied at pod creation (09:45:09Z), after the five MutatingWebhookConfigurations were created at 09:45:01Z selecting namespace social-network and pointing at service platform-policy-controller.platform-ops:/mutate. The load generator addressing the nginx-thrift ClusterIP 10.96.80.225 saw socket write errors jump from 4 (round ending 09:45:07Z) to 68832 (round ending 09:45:18Z). All other 26 social-network pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts, their Deployments report 1/1 ready, and the sampled traces up to 09:45:09Z show HTTP 200 from nginx-web-server with no error spans in the downstream services, so the failure observed here is confined to the front end and no downstream service is shown to be failing. The SIGKILL-by-memory-limit mechanism is inferred from exit 137 and the injected 16Mi limit; no OOMKilled reason and no cAdvisor memory/OOM series for that pod or node exist in the window.

claims.text: Deployment nginx-thrift is at generation 2 / revision 2, with helm Apply at 2026-11-24T09:44:47Z and a kubectl-patch Update at 2026-11-24T09:44:57Z; its pod template declares container nginx-thrift requests.memory=128Mi and limits.memory=256Mi for image ghcr.io/sregym/openresty-thrift:20261109-trace-identity.

The superseded ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df (deployment revision 1) specified container resources {} (no memory request or limit) while the new ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 (revision 2) specifies requests 128Mi / limits 256Mi; both reference the identical image digest, so the resources block is the template delta introduced by the 09:44:57 patch.

Five MutatingWebhookConfigurations (cert-manager-webhook, gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration, istio-sidecar-injector, kyverno-resource-mutating-webhook-cfg, linkerd-proxy-injector-webhook-config) were created at 2026-11-24T09:45:01Z; all of them send admission to service platform-policy-controller in namespace platform-ops, path /mutate port 443, and select namespace kubernetes.io/metadata.name=social-network. The gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration webhook is the one whose rule matches apiGroups [""] resources ["pods"], operation CREATE, scope Namespaced, with an empty objectSelector, so it applies to every pod created in social-network.

ConfigMap platform-ops/platform-policy-controller-server contains server.py with the constant MEMORY = "16Mi" and a build_patch() function that emits JSON-Patch operations writing MEMORY into container[0] resources.requests.memory and resources.limits.memory (replacing existing values), returned as the AdmissionReview patch.

Deployment platform-ops/platform-policy-controller (created 2026-11-24T09:44:59Z) runs container command python /app/server.py (image python:3.12-alpine) and mounts ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server at /app, i.e. it is the backend serving those webhook configurations.

Pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-dw5sd (created 2026-11-24T09:45:09Z) has container nginx-thrift with resources requests.memory=16Mi and limits.memory=16Mi, although its owning ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 declares 128Mi/256Mi; the pod-level 16Mi matches the value the platform-policy-controller webhook injects.

Across all 27 pods in namespace social-network, nginx-thrift-65f656c999-dw5sd (created 09:45:09Z, after the webhooks appeared at 09:45:01Z) is the only pod that has any memory limit (limits=requests=16Mi); all other 26 pods, created 09:44:47-09:44:53Z, have no memory limit and no memory request.

The nginx-thrift container of pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-dw5sd terminated twice with exitCode 137 (started 09:45:11Z finished 09:45:15Z; started 09:45:16Z finished 09:45:19Z), reason Error, restartCount 1, and the pod's Ready and ContainersReady conditions are False with reason ContainersNotReady; kubelet recorded Warning BackOff "Back-off restarting failed container nginx-thrift in pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-dw5sd" at 09:45:19Z.
The Endpoints object for Service nginx-thrift contains only notReadyAddresses (pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-dw5sd, IP 10.244.234.160, port 8080) and no ready address.
Service nginx-thrift is ClusterIP 10.96.80.225, port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, which is the address the load generator used (http://10.96.80.225:8080/wrk2-api/post/compose).

Load generator pod wrk2-job-h4n6b reported for its 10 s round ending 09:45:07Z "1021 requests in 10.00s" and "Socket errors: connect 0, read 0, write 4", and for the round ending 09:45:18Z "717 requests in 10.00s" and "Socket errors: connect 0, read 202, write 68832".

In the sampled traces for 09:45:01.709Z-09:45:09.346Z, nginx-web-server spans /wrk2-api/post/compose, /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read and /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read all carry http.status_code=200 with zero error rows, and the spans of compose-post-service, text-service, user-mention-service, url-shorten-service, post-storage-service, home-timeline-service, user-timeline-service, social-graph-service, media-service, unique-id-service and user-service show no error status.

nginx-thrift container stderr logs record "worker process N exited on signal 11" at 09:44:59Z for pod nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df-s8bl6 (the pre-patch pod without a memory limit) and at 09:45:09Z and 09:45:18Z for pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-dwv7m.

Every other social-network Deployment reports spec.replicas=1 with readyReplicas=1 and availableReplicas=1, while nginx-thrift reports no readyReplicas/availableReplicas with generation 2 and updatedReplicas=1; all other 26 pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts.

container_oom_events_total for namespace social-network was 0 at 2026-11-24T09:45:20Z for every container it reported and no series existed for pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-dw5sd, so no OOM counter exists for the crashing container.

The 16Mi memory limit injected by the platform-policy-controller webhook drove the openresty-thrift container over its cgroup memory limit, so the kernel/kubelet killed it (exit 137 = 128+SIGKILL) about 4 s after each start, producing a crash loop, empty nginx-thrift endpoints and a front-end outage; this is inferred from exit 137, from the injected limit being the only difference between this pod and the 26 healthy pods, and from the ~4 s lifetime of each attempt, because no OOMKilled termination reason and no container_oom_events_total series for this pod were observed.

The failures are confined to the front end: all 26 other pods in social-network are Running and Ready with 0 restarts, all their Deployments report 1 ready/1 available, and the sampled traces of every downstream service show HTTP 200 / no error spans up to 09:45:09Z, so no downstream service is shown to be broken by this cause.

The 256Mi limit added to the nginx-thrift Deployment template by the 09:44:57 kubectl-patch is not the cause of the crash loop: the running pod's effective limit is 16Mi, not the 256Mi in the revision-2 ReplicaSet template, and the only other pod built from that same template (nginx-thrift-65f656c999-dwv7m) was created before the webhooks existed at 09:45:01Z.

The nginx worker SIGSEGV messages ("worker process N exited on signal 11") are not accepted as the cause of the outage: the same message appears for pod nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df-s8bl6, which was the pre-patch pod without a memory limit, while the container's own exit code on both observed terminations of pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-dw5sd is 137 (SIGKILL).

gaps: The OOM kill is not directly observed: the container termination reason is "Error" (not OOMKilled), and the queries for container_oom_events_total (no series for pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-dw5sd) and container_memory_working_set_bytes/container_memory_usage_bytes for pod=~"nginx-thrift.*" returned nothing (no_data), so the 16Mi limit is tied to exit 137 by inference, not by an OOM record.
The platform-policy-controller pod log query for 09:40:00-09:45:20Z returned zero lines (its handler overrides log_message), so there is no server-side record of which admission requests it mutated.

Change history is not integrated in this Run (not_integrated: change_history); managedFields name only kubectl-client-side-apply (platform-policy-controller deployment) and OpenAPI-Generator (the five webhook configurations), so who created them and why cannot be established.

Why pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-dwv7m was stopped at 09:45:09Z is unknown: only a kubelet "Stopping container nginx-thrift" event was captured; no SuccessfulDelete event for it appeared in the window.

LimitRange objects cannot be read with the available tool kind list, so a namespace default limit as an alternative source of the 16Mi value is unchecked (the value matches the webhook ConfigMap's MEMORY constant exactly).

A trace query for nginx-web-server spans in 09:45:10-09:45:20Z returned no data, so whether any request was served after 09:45:09Z is unknown, and the trace view used here is incomplete (backend returned as many traces as requested) and covers only 09:45:01.709Z-09:45:09.346Z.

The wrk2 log query for 09:44:00-09:45:20Z was incomplete (80-line limit) and the query for 09:44:30-09:45:20Z showed a reconnect_socket flood at 09:45:19.99Z, but per-round summary lines outside those windows were not retrieved.

Prometheus queries for kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total, kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready and node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes returned no data at 09:45:20Z, so pod-restart and node-memory series could not be cross-checked.
Post-09:45:20Z state is outside the authorized window: whether the 16Mi injection persisted, whether the webhooks still exist, and whether the pod recovered cannot be determined.
Impact beyond the in-cluster load generator (external or real users) is unverified; no user-facing telemetry is available.
next_steps: Remove or correct the mutating admission webhooks in platform-ops that select namespace social-network (notably gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration) and/or fix MEMORY in ConfigMap platform-ops/platform-policy-controller-server, since MEMORY="16Mi" is stamped into requests and limits of container[0] for every new pod in that namespace.

After the webhook is corrected, delete pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-dw5sd so it is re-admitted, then confirm the new pod's limits equal the Deployment's 128Mi/256Mi and that the nginx-thrift Endpoints has a ready address.
Re-verify the intended 128Mi/256Mi resources applied to the nginx-thrift Deployment at 09:44:57Z and check whether that patch was part of the same faulty change.

Review audit/change history for the creation of the five MutatingWebhookConfigurations at 2026-11-24T09:45:01Z and of Deployment platform-ops/platform-policy-controller at 09:44:59Z to identify the actor.
Enable kubelet/cAdvisor recording of OOM kills and container memory for node sregym-worker so OOMKilled events can be confirmed directly.

import base64
import json
import ssl
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

MEMORY = "16Mi"

def build_patch(resources):
    """Emit JSON Patch ops that stamp MEMORY into both
    resources.requests.memory and resources.limits.memory on container[0].
    RFC 6902 "add" semantics: replaces the value if the target already exists,
    so this works whether the field is absent or already populated."""
    ops = []
    if resources is None:
        ops.append({
            "op": "add",
            "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources",
            "value": {"requests": {"memory": MEMORY}, "limits": {"memory": MEMORY}},
        })
        return ops
    if resources.get("requests") is None:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/requests",
                    "value": {"memory": MEMORY}})
    else:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory",
                    "value": MEMORY})
    if resources.get("limits") is None:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/limits",
                    "value": {"memory": MEMORY}})
    else:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory",
                    "value": MEMORY})
    return ops

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("content-length", "0") or 0)
        raw = self.rfile.read(length)
        uid = ""
        patch = []
        try:
            body = json.loads(raw)
            uid = body.get("request", {}).get("uid", "")
            containers = body.get("request", {}).get("object", {}).get("spec", {}).get("containers", [])
            if containers:
                patch = build_patch(containers[0].get("resources"))
        except Exception:
            pass

        resp = {"uid": uid, "allowed": True}
        if patch:
            resp["patchType"] = "JSONPatch"
            resp["patch"] = base64.b64encode(json.dumps(patch).encode()).decode()
        response = {
            "apiVersion": "admission.k8s.io/v1",
            "kind": "AdmissionReview",
            "response": resp,
        }
        data = json.dumps(response).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)

    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):
        return

httpd = HTTPServer(("0.0.0.0", 8443), Handler)
ctx = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER)
ctx.load_cert_chain("/certs/tls.crt", "/certs/tls.key")
httpd.socket = ctx.wrap_socket(httpd.socket, server_side=True)
httpd.serve_forever()
